To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the treatment of non- professional suretyship agreements in the EU is characterized by diverging approaches that can be seen in terms of elements of commonality in a unitary network.

there is a Tower of Babel of national approaches to the law of non-professional (or non-commercial) suretyship, but that this Tower is built on a Unitary Network of commonalities that may be exploited to bring about judicial convergence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent to which a common core is emerging from the Tower of Babel in the field of non-professional (or 'personal') suretyship.
the question of how the EU's internal market for financial services is being constructed in relation to non-professional sureties and the role of national courts in this process.
the extent to which the surety relationship is being harmonised in a common core of European private law, and the implications for the future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Tower of Babel is not a Tower of Babel after all.
the Tower is being transformed into a Unitary Network.
the Tower of Babel will not be demolished.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the suretyship field is an example of how the 'common core' and 'Tower of Bable' models are not mutually exclusive, but may co-exist in a Unitary Network.
, while the EU has been unable to achieve a common core of surety protection, it has been able to achieve a common framework for surety protection.
the Tower of Babel is not the only option.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the European Commission's efforts to date have been insufficient to achieve either of its aims.

the suretyship agreement is not a suitable vehicle to achieve a single market in European financial services, but it may well provide a useful model for achieving a single market in the field of European private law.
the European Union is not a Tower of Babel, but a Unitary Network.
